items.title: Eisenkot Accuses Netanyahu of Fueling ‘Racist’ Hostility Against Arabs
items.summary: Gadi Eisenkot sharply criticized Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu days after the Israeli leader attacked Arab lawmakers in a divisive speech.
items.full_text: Gadi Eisenkot, the former military chief who is trying to form the next Israeli government, accused Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Friday of fueling a “racist” campaign against the country’s Arab citizens, in some of the strongest public criticism of his rival’s attacks on the community. The comments were made days after Mr. Netanyahu delivered a divisive speech to the opening session of Parliament, or the Knesset, in which he referred to Arab lawmakers as “terror supporters” and “haters of Israel.” Diplomats and analysts condemned the remarks as a brazen display of hatred and incitement against Arab citizens, who make up about 20 percent of the overall population, and voted in massive numbers in inconclusive elections last month. “Since the beginning of the election campaign, they have been subjected to a racist and aggressive campaign of delegitimization, fueled by the outgoing prime minister and those around him for political purposes,” Mr. Eisenkot said in a statement on social media. “Arab citizens of Israel are an integral part of the Israeli story,” he said, adding that it was wrong to malign an entire community. “The attempt to marginalize them and vilify them collectively is a profound violation of the principles of statesmanship,” Mr. Eisenkot said. “It dishonors Israel’s Declaration of Independence and the values we take pride in as a Jewish and democratic state.” The Declaration of Independence says all citizens have equal social and political rights “irrespective of religion, race or sex.” Thank you for your patience while we verify access. items.title: Caught Between Killers: Ebola on One Side, Islamic State on the Other
items.summary: The new epicenter of Congo’s fast-spreading outbreak is a region scarred by rebel violence. Responders are struggling to help it.
items.full_text: Six months on, Ebola continues to hack a deadly trail across eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. When the outbreak was first detected in May, it resembled a single, giant blaze, with infections concentrated in a handful of towns in one province. It has since morphed into a far bigger, more elusive foe, creeping into eight provinces and splintering into numerous hot spots as it moves through one of the world’s great rainforests. Instead of one big fire, there are many now, scattered across a vast area about the size of Britain. Health workers have corralled the virus where it was first detected, but infections are soaring elsewhere. Biakato, a small town deep in the rainforest, suddenly accounted for as many as one-quarter of new cases nationally. Yet its beleaguered residents were left almost entirely on their own, with dangerously little to defend themselves against the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history . “We see the same mistakes as before,” said Dr. Jean-Jacques Muyembe, who helped discover Ebola in 1976 and now heads Congo’s National Institute for Biomedical Research. “It’s as if we were starting from zero. It’s very disappointing.” And if that were not enough, the campaign to contain the epidemic has run into a terrifying new threat: the Islamic State.

items.title: The U.S.-Israel Relationship Is Broken. Here’s How Eisenkot Could Fix It.
items.summary: Former Israeli and U.S. ambassadors, lawmakers and analysts largely agree on steps Gadi Eisenkot could take if he becomes prime minister. But they are risky.
items.full_text: Gadi Eisenkot, the former military chief who has been given a chance to form Israel’s new governing coalition and replace Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, is by no means assured of success. But if he does take power, another hugely daunting challenge would immediately confront him: how to undo the vast damage done to Israel’s relationship with the United States, its closest and most important ally. It’s hard to imagine things getting much worse. Many Americans have turned against Israel over its devastating military campaign in Gaza, and even more so over its role in pressing for war with Iran , which led to soaring gas prices. President Trump announced this month that he would cut off billions of dollars in annual U.S. military aid to Israel by the end of the year and blamed Israel in part for Republican losses in the midterm elections. Democratic control of Congress could quickly lead to sanctions on violent Israeli settlers and on new settlement construction in the occupied West Bank, as well as to new conditions on arms sales. In the past, Israel could always turn to Congress for support in clashes with the White House, said Michael Oren, a former Israeli ambassador to Washington and deputy prime minister under Mr. Netanyahu. But no longer. “For the first time in the history of our relationship with the United States, we have no recourse,” he said. “We have to start from scratch. We have a lot of fence mending to do and with no guarantee of success. Zero.” Thank you for your patience while we verify access. items.title: Study Hard, Get a Career and Get Ahead? It’s Not What It Used to Be.
items.summary: From India to France, the implicit meritocratic bargain that underwrote stable societies by providing advancement to new generations is breaking down.
items.full_text: Protest movements have long relied on students as some of the most ardent foot soldiers. Young people have been on the front lines of protests against war, climate change and racial inequality. But in huge protests that have shaken India and France this fall, students have revolted against the failed promises of education itself. In India, students took to the streets after the government abruptly canceled the results of a medical-school admissions exam because test questions had been leaked online. Aspiring doctors had to take the test again, after many spent years studying for up to 12 hours a day in hopes of winning one of the coveted spots — and the chance of upward mobility. Young people across the country saw the scandal as emblematic of a broken education system and were furious. In France, students in poor suburbs outside Paris began protesting the decrepit physical condition of their schools, an opaque university admissions system and absent teachers. French education had long promised to serve as a “social elevator” enabling young people to advance in society, but had fallen into disrepair. Soon, demonstrations spread across the country and, in some cities, spiraled into rioting. In both countries, the anger of the students shows no signs of abating. And while in many ways France and India could hardly be more different, their unrest was sparked by a similar source of outrage: the breakdown of a foundational social contract that one could call the meritocratic bargain. It is a promise that lies at the core of many countries’ political compacts. Though specifics can vary, the central proposition usually goes something like this: A fair society rewards merit. Educational achievements are a good measure of merit because education is open to all and leads to valuable skills. Therefore, education should be a route to social and economic advancement. The value of this system is not just that it selects for those with high ability, but also that it offers a justification for the resulting socioeconomic hierarchy — including who ends up at the bottom. “All selection mechanisms generate losers,” said Nicholas Kuipers, a professor at Princeton University who studies the politics of meritocracy. “The question is, Who do you want to be a loser, and who do you want to be a winner?” Thank you for your patience while we verify access. items.title: Europe Agrees on a Team to Represent It in Talks With Russia
items.summary: After coveting a seat in the Ukraine war discussions, Europe is poised to get one. The continent wants to fill it with a six-member team.
items.full_text: European leaders have waited on the margins of negotiations to end Russia’s war in Ukraine for months, eyeing a seat at the table. They learned this week that they would get one, and simply needed to decide which official should sit in that chair. Instead, they decided on six. European Union leaders concluded in Dublin on Friday that they will tap a group of major nations — Britain, France, Germany, Poland, and Italy — along with a representative from the E.U’s leadership arms, the European Council and European Commission. In some ways, the choice of a crowd plays into jibes Americans have made about the continent’s indecisiveness: “If Europe could identify one person to speak on their behalf, that would be a bigger achievement than getting the Russians to include them in the negotiation,” Jared Kushner, President Trump’s son-in-law and a U.S. envoy, said earlier this week. Europe’s failure to pick one negotiator leaves open the possibility that its fragmentation will diminish its influence. Even so, Europeans have underscored that they are a democracy of many nations, though, and that many voices must be represented. “We decide on who represents us, and that is what we have done today,” said Ursula von der Leyen, the president of the European Commission. “We need to work as a team,” António Costa, president of the European Union’s political leadership arm, said at a news conference on Friday, noting that America itself has two envoys. items.title: After Xi Purges China’s Generals, a Military Inquisitor Rises
items.summary: The rise of Zhang Shengmin suggests that China’s top brass remains embroiled in investigations, potentially complicating preparations for war over Taiwan.
items.full_text: When China’s leader, Xi Jinping, endorsed the expulsion of dozens of disgraced officials at a recent Communist Party meeting in Beijing, one man stood out as a clear winner. Taking his new place at the front of the meeting was Gen. Zhang Shengmin, the somber-faced enforcer of Mr. Xi’s purges inside the military. He had been promoted to the Politburo, the party’s top leadership council, the latest step in his improbable rise from low-profile inspector to a position second only to Mr. Xi in China’s military hierarchy. General Zhang has been the principal overseer of Mr. Xi’s campaign to purify the People’s Liberation Army. His latest elevation signaled that the investigations, indoctrination drives and loyalty tests could continue for years, as Mr. Xi searches for officers he believes are irreproachably loyal, experts and officials said. “Twist the blade inward, with strict measures to cure disorder,” China’s main military newspaper said after the party meeting that was held late last month, referring to the continued discipline campaign. Three officials in Taiwan said they believed Mr. Xi’s loyalty campaign would keep the Chinese military focused on its own problems. That could hinder preparations for possible war over Taiwan, the self-governed island democracy that Beijing claims. The officials spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss internal assessments. The leadership uncertainty comes as China’s military has continued to pressure Taiwan. Dozens of P.L.A. ships held unannounced drills in seas off the Chinese coast in recent weeks, with some, including a carrier strike group, still remaining, Joseph Wu , the secretary-general of Taiwan’s National Security Council, posted on X on Thursday. items.title: Border Crossings Have Plummeted. Stephen Miller Isn’t Satisfied.
items.summary: Mexico has cooperated to significantly slow the flow of migrants. The new White House chief of staff insists it is not enough.
items.full_text: Since President Trump resumed office, the number of illegal crossings at the U.S.-Mexico border has dropped to the lowest point in decades. For one of Mr. Trump’s top policy advisers, that is not enough. In conversations with both American and Mexican officials over the last several months, Stephen Miller has insisted that illegal border crossings must be reduced, according to officials in both countries familiar with the private conversations but not authorized to discuss them. Mr. Miller’s goal, they said, is zero crossings. Mexican officials have said that, with a nearly 2,000-mile border, that is simply not possible. In his new role as chief of staff, Mr. Miller is expected to continue driving that agenda. One of the main forums for Mr. Miller’s demands has been his near daily calls with the U.S. ambassador to Mexico, Ronald ​Johnson, some of the officials said. On calls with staff, Mr. Miller, previously the deputy chief of staff, frequently rails about the number of border crossings, despite their low figures, the officials said. That has been especially true in recent months, they said, as border crossings increased slightly, to the highest point in Mr. Trump’s second term.

items.title: One of France’s Most Popular Athletes Is Running for President
items.summary: Centrists want alternatives to a matchup between the far right and far left in the 2027 presidential race. Enter Christine Lagarde, a former central banker — and Teddy Riner, a judo star.
items.full_text: When Teddy Riner, a judo champion and one of France’s most popular athletes, announced this week that he would run for president, it was less a game changer than a welcome diversion. For all of his appeal, Mr. Riner, 37, is unlikely to win the race to replace President Emmanuel Macron next spring. Yet his quixotic candidacy reveals a hard truth about France’s presidential campaign. Five months before voters go to the polls, many are eager, even desperate, for a fresh face to upend a race that looks increasingly as if it’s on a glide path to the election of France’s first far-right government since World War II. The main far-right candidate, Marine Le Pen, has held a commanding lead over all her rivals for months — a lead that has only been reinforced by weeks of protests, marred by violence, that have shaken France. The most prominent center-right candidate, Édouard Philippe, has faded in the polls as the unrest has sharpened the appeal of far-right calls for law and order and left-wing calls for social justice. Another beneficiary of the upheaval is a far-left firebrand, Jean-Luc Mélenchon, who now appears to be the likeliest candidate to advance into a second round against Ms. Le Pen in France’s two-round system. As things currently stand, French voters would be confronted with a choice between two poles of the political spectrum. Centrist voters are “afraid of being confronted with a duel between Marine Le Pen and Jean-Luc Mélenchon,” said Jean-Daniel Lévy, deputy director of Toluna France, a polling firm. These voters, he said, are an “orphan electorate,” lacking an inspiring candidate, and are “still looking for someone.” Raphaël LLorca, an analyst at the Jean-Jaurès Foundation, a left-leaning research group in Paris, said the search for a white knight showed “the panic of the centrist bloc.” He added, “It is clear that the election is slipping away from them.” Thank you for your patience while we verify access. items.title: In Moscow, Witkoff and Kushner Ask Putin to Include Europe in Peace Talks
items.summary: In Dublin, President Volodymyr Zelensky of Ukraine said Europeans would join the next round of talks. Russia has not confirmed that.
items.full_text: President Trump’s envoys went to Moscow on Thursday to seek agreement from President Vladimir V. Putin to bring Europe into talks on the war in Ukraine, as the Kremlin pushes to widen the negotiations to overhaul European security arrangements. The envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, arrived in Russia one day after mediating peace talks in Abu Dhabi between Russian and Ukrainian representatives, who spoke directly for the first time in nine months. After meeting with Mr. Putin in the Kremlin, they traveled to Dublin to meet with and debrief President Volodymyr Zelensky of Ukraine. Mr. Witkoff and Mr. Kushner are pressing to involve Europe in the talks as Russia makes clear that it will not consider a cease-fire until its broader demands to redraw Europe’s security architecture are addressed. “We cannot conclude this deal without Europeans being at the table,” Mr. Kushner told reporters on Thursday night, speaking at the air base where he and Mr. Witkoff had just met with Mr. Zelensky, as planes for both delegations waited nearby. Mr. Zelensky, standing next to him, said that Europe will join the next round of talks. “It’s important for us, because the war is in Europe,” he said. The Trump administration, seeking a foreign policy win after Republicans’ drubbing in the midterm elections, is making another push for peace even as Russia gives no indication that it will stop the war anytime soon, and in fact appears to be hardening some positions. items.title: A.I. Weapons Need Data for Their Training. Ukraine Has a Lot to Offer.
items.summary: The Ukrainian government has opened up a trove of five million battlefield videos to defense companies at home and abroad.
items.full_text: The forest, seen from a drone, appeared as a vast, monotonous landscape of black tree trunks, shadows and patches of snow. To the human eye, it appeared deserted. But to an artificial intelligence system looking for people, it did not. The system put a red box around a tiny human form, probably a soldier lurking in the trees. Behind this feat lay vast volumes of data. Just as ChatGPT and other A.I. chatbots must be exposed to how humans write, military A.I. systems must be exposed to how humans fight. In Ukraine, this happens through a huge trove of battlefield videos, audio and text data collected over nearly five years. The war database is being used by about 30 Ukrainian defense companies to develop A.I. weapons. Ukraine is now opening this repository, which it calls Avenger Labs, to firms in allied countries, hoping to deepen security partnerships. Ukraine is providing the data at no charge, but companies must give the Ukrainian military licenses to any software they develop. Under the first agreement to be reached, 12 British defense companies will gain access. Ukraine is in talks with other countries. While there is no shortage of Western companies developing autonomous weapons, there is a shortage of the data needed to train them. Ukraine can offer more of it than any other potential partner. items.title: Microsoft’s Global Outage and Fixes: What We Know
items.summary: The company described “encouraging” progress on efforts to overcome a second day of disruptions to its email, messaging and other services.
items.full_text: Microsoft is reporting widespread improvements to its services after a global outage took them offline on Thursday, disrupting communications and work at schools, government agencies and offices around the world. The company, headquartered in Redmond, Wash., said on Friday that it was seeing “encouraging recovery progress, with service availability and email delivery performance improving across a growing portion of affected infrastructure.” “We remain focused on addressing residual impact and ensuring reliable service restoration,” the company added. Here’s what to know as of Friday afternoon. What happened? Outages started disrupting Microsoft tools and apps around noon Eastern time on Thursday and quickly spread to more than 70 countries and territories, affecting millions of users, according to Downdetector , an outage-tracking site. Some of Microsoft’s most popular products, including the email manager Outlook, the workplace messaging and video calling app Teams and the artificial intelligence assistant Copilot, stopped working. Was this a cyberattack? Microsoft said in a statement on Friday that “for now, we can confirm that there is no indication this is the result of malicious or cyber activity.” It added that the problem was “a technical issue not related to cyber or A.I.” agents. So why were Microsoft’s systems not working? The company has yet to provide a clear answer, although it has promised to make public a full report that identifies the “root cause” of the outage. items.title: Asian Americans Share Disappointment and Fear After Jensen Huang Scandal
items.summary: Many East Asians said that he had swagger and seemed like a superhero. Now there are worries that the spy scandal turns into hyper scrutiny against them.
items.full_text: Jensen Huang’s ouster from Nvidia has prompted fears about its plunging stock, China’s espionage efforts and the future of America’s A.I. competitiveness. But for some Asian Americans, especially those of Chinese and Taiwanese descent working in technology, the rapid downfall of the powerful C.E.O. has come with another layer of disappointment, as well as fear. To many, Mr. Huang was a hero — one of the few who smashed through the bamboo ceiling that has long stymied many Asian and Asian American professionals from reaching the C-suite, and did so with an energy that defied stereotypes of Asian Americans as timid or complacent in the workplace. “He had a swagger,” said Dave Lu, managing partner of Hyphen Capital and a Taiwanese American veteran of Silicon Valley. “To see that exemplified was very inspirational.” Mr. Lu said that he had been fielding messages from Asian and Asian American tech executives ever since The New York Times reported that Mr. Huang, the Taiwanese American chief executive of Nvidia, had an extramarital affair with a woman that U.S. intelligence services believe to be a Chinese spy. Nvidia’s board has opened an investigation into his conduct, and Mr. Huang resigned from the company on Thursday. President Trump said Monday that Mr. Huang told him that he was unaware that the woman was an intelligence operative for Beijing. Thank you for your patience while we verify access. items.title: Wall Street Loses a Powerful Dealmaker After Nvidia’s CEO Is Ousted
items.summary: The ousted Nvidia chief executive was the consummate dealmaker leading the trillion-dollar A.I. build out.
items.full_text: With Jensen Huang’s abrupt ouster from Nvidia, Wall Street has lost its most powerful and profitable dealmaker. As Mr. Huang built Nvidia from a regional chipmaker into the world’s largest company, he dispensed with the usual careful, corporate hand-wringing. He personally directed splashy deals and complicated financing structures that pumped hundreds of billions of dollars into would-be competitors, suppliers and customers. If that made him, in the public eye, a face of the global A.I. build out, on Wall Street he represented something else: manna. His deals produced billions of dollars in fees for banks, asset managers and advisers, and Nvidia was, up until this week, spending or promising money at a speed and magnitude of little precedence. Now Wall Street bankers, traders and even some of Nvidia’s competitors are wondering and worrying about whether Mr. Huang’s departure will slow the breakneck pace of Nvidia’s investments. Some say that the fundamentals of Nvidia’s power are still intact, like its extreme control of the global supply of chips, the A.I. boom’s scarcest resource, the company’s deep cash coffers and the Trump administration’s warm support for the industry’s regulatory agenda. But Mr. Huang was the leader who harnessed all of those assets into a deal-making machine. “Nvidia is the central bank of A.I.,” said Michael Edwards, director of Forum Markets, an A.I.-focused merchant bank. “Imagine the Fed without a chairman.” Thank you for your patience while we verify access. items.title: Bessent Faults Commerce Dept. for Failing to Blacklist Megaspeed
items.summary: The Treasury secretary blamed the department for not sanctioning the Singaporean firm and said that Nvidia employees should be held accountable if they sidestepped the law.
items.full_text: Scott Bessent, the Treasury secretary, blamed the Commerce Department on Friday for the government’s failure to sanction the Singaporean data center firm Megaspeed, saying that other departments had pushed for the measure but that Commerce “has the pen.” The Treasury, Defense and State Departments and the U.S. trade representative were all in favor of putting Megaspeed on a trade blacklist called the entity list for months, but the Commerce Department is in charge of that authority, Mr. Bessent said on CNBC on Friday. “You will have to ask them about their internal processes,” he said, adding, “Treasury and my deputy has been pushing for this for months at the deputies level.” “The real story here should be: Did Nvidia know their client, and was there a robust effort at Nvidia to make sure that there was no leakage and that they were selling to what were obviously pass-through shell companies?” he said. “I think it’s important that anyone at the company there be held accountable for that.” Frustration is boiling over within the administration and on Capitol Hill about Megaspeed, the company led by a woman U.S. intelligence deemed to be an asset for the Chinese government. The woman, Alice Huang, had a relationship with Nvidia’s chief executive, Jensen Huang. Mr. Huang resigned from his company on Thursday in the wake of revelations about that and another affair, sending the company’s stock price cratering. items.title: Jensen Huang’s Resignation From Nvidia Worries the A.I. Start-Up World
items.summary: Mr. Huang championed start-ups, with Nvidia holding $48 billion worth of stakes in 229 private companies, including OpenAI and Anthropic, at the end of July.
items.full_text: For years, Jensen Huang was a frequent presence at Silicon Valley start-up events, networking with founders, judging pitch competitions and showing up at “demo” days. The Nvidia chief executive became a godlike figure in the start-up ecosystem, not just because the industry idolized him as one of the world’s most successful entrepreneurs. Mr. Huang, 63, also made it his mission to help start-ups gain a foothold against the industry’s biggest and most powerful tech companies, providing funding and computing power. “As many good ideas as we have, you don’t have all the world’s good ideas,” he said on the Acquired podcast in 2023. So Mr. Huang’s abrupt resignation from Nvidia on Thursday has investors and start-up founders nervous that they have lost a powerful ally. “Nvidia is the central bank of A.I. and all of a sudden, the Fed chairman is out,” said Tomasz Tunguz, an investor at Theory Ventures, which funds young start-ups. Nvidia held $48 billion worth of stakes in 229 private companies, including large stakes in OpenAI and Anthropic, at the end of July, according to securities filings. It more than doubled its start-up investments in six months. Thank you for your patience while we verify access. items.title: Fewer Fed Meetings Raise Stakes of Warsh’s Communications
items.summary: The Federal Reserve will vote on interest rates less frequently beginning next year as part of a plan by the central bank’s chairman, Kevin M. Warsh, to overhaul how it operates.
items.full_text: When officials at the Federal Reserve meet next month to vote on interest rates, they will have only a partial snapshot of the economy in hand. Fresh inflation data comes out the day after policymakers finalize their rate decision, leaving them without insight into whether price pressures in November continued to accelerate or showed signs of easing. This predicament underscores why officials at the central bank broadly appear on board with a plan hatched by Kevin M. Warsh, the Fed chairman, to reduce the number of meetings convened each year to vote on interest rates. The changes will be ushered in gradually, beginning next fall. In a revised schedule released on Thursday , the Fed confirmed that its policymakers will meet eight times in 2027, but that the Oct. 25-26 gathering will be “dedicated to the discussion of broad monetary policy strategy issues.” By 2028, there will be just six meetings accompanied by policy votes, with two others focused on strategy. Meeting less frequently, and at more evenly spaced intervals, has the clear benefit of giving officials a more consistent flow of economic data to parse when they gather to debate their policy settings. But there are trade-offs that will put more onus on Mr. Warsh to communicate openly about how the Fed is approaching its rate decisions and its thinking about the outlook, something he has so far resisted even as the central bank has embarked on raising rates this year. “The decision process is more important than the timing,” said Esther George, who served as president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City from 2011 to 2023. “And this committee is struggling a bit with how to communicate what exactly they mean.” Thank you for your patience while we verify access. items.title: Deed Theft Is Rising, Along With Property Values
items.summary: The victims are often older people or immigrants, with thieves going after vacant land or unoccupied homes. But there are ways to protect yourself.
items.full_text: A dying woman with dementia. A doctor from Long Island. A couple renovating a home in Florida. The three fell victim to a type of real estate fraud known as deed, or title, theft, in which someone forges documents or fakes an identity to take ownership of a home or vacant land. Criminals may impersonate the true owners and sell the property to unsuspecting buyers, or use it as collateral to obtain loans. The rise in home property values, and, therefore, home equity , have made deed theft potentially lucrative, experts say. Homes owned by older people, homes that show signs of financial distress, and vacant homes or land may be especially vulnerable. It’s not clear how common deed theft is nationally but awareness of the fraud is mounting, especially in the Northeast. Earlier this month, a Queens man became the first person convicted under a New York deed theft law passed in 2024. And New York City has created a special office of deed theft prevention to detect and investigate such fraud. Reports of real estate crime in general rose by 32 percent in 2025, to more than 12,000 complaints, and associated financial losses rose to more than $275 million, according to the F.B.I.’s Internet Crime Complaint Center. The F.B.I. estimates it received 66 complaints about deed or title theft in 2025, representing $5.9 million in losses, compared with 75 complaints representing losses of almost $7 million from January through October of this year. The National Association of Realtors surveyed real-estate executives nationally in 2025 and found that nearly two-thirds reported being aware of this type of fraud in their area within the past year, with awareness highest — 95 percent — in the Northeast. But the fraud isn’t confined to one region. “It happens everywhere,” said Craig Haskins, president of the American Land Title Association, a trade group for title insurers and agents and real-estate closing professionals. The group’s survey this year of 245 title professionals in 40 states found that nearly three out of five had experienced at least one incident of attempted “seller impersonation” fraud, up from about a quarter two years earlier. items.title: A Scorecard for Huang’s Exit From Nvidia
items.summary: The ouster of Jensen Huang from the chipmaker he helped found is reverberating throughout Silicon Valley, Washington and beyond.
items.full_text: Andrew here. The Nvidia soap opera continues. The Wall Street Journal reports that Jensen Huang belittled Colette Kress , then the chipmaker’s C.F.O. and now his interim replacement as C.E.O. (One question: what Kress’s ascension means for Huang’s children and son-in-law, all of whom are executives at Nvidia — and some of whom have clashed with her , according to The Information.) All this paints an increasingly complicated picture for Nvidia and for Huang, who has been called to testify before Congress. More below. Winners and losers The central figure of the artificial intelligence boom, Jensen Huang , is out as Nvidia’s C.E.O. Executives, investors and policymakers are trying to sort through the wreckage. Nvidia is being led on an interim basis by its C.F.O., Colette Kress , who must steer the company through increasingly fraught times for the A.I. industry. (More on that below.) Huang’s resignation is continuing to reverberate throughout Silicon Valley and Washington. The latest: Shares in Nvidia are up in premarket trading after falling as much as 14 percent on Thursday. Beyond Alice Huang , the chip executive whom U.S. intelligence concluded was a Chinese spy, and Kimberly Powell , a direct subordinate, Huang had an affair with another Nvidia employee , Reuters reports, citing unnamed sources. The famously energetic Huang appeared defeated by on Thursday as the toll of the scandal grew, Bloomberg reports, citing unnamed sources. Details are still emerging about Alice Huang, whose cloud-computing company Megaspeed, based in Singapore, has been accused of smuggling Nvidia chips into China. Researchers and government officials are dissecting her involvement in a tangled web of companies that may have included Huawei , the Chinese chip giant blacklisted by the U.S., and DeepSeek , the Chinese A.I. powerhouse. That said, some U.S. intelligence officials have suggested they haven’t yet concluded that Alice Huang was a spy. Some in Silicon Valley are set to benefit from Nvidia’s distress. Chief among them are rival chipmakers who have tried to wean A.I. companies off Nvidia’s GPU processors. Shares in Broadcom (which has been developing a custom A.I. chip with OpenAI) and AMD jumped 5 percent on Thursday, though they’re set to give up some of those gains on Friday. items.title: Jensen Huang’s Fall Costs Asia an A.I. Ambassador to the U.S.
items.summary: The ex-Nvidia C.E.O. was a bridge between companies and governments. His exit will reverberate, especially in China where it could accelerate a self-reliance drive.
items.full_text: In Indonesia, Jensen Huang was called the leader of the artificial intelligence revolution. In Japan, he was “the next Steve Jobs,” according to the technology investor Masayoshi Son. In Taiwan, where he was born, he is just called Dad. Mr. Huang, who resigned this week from the powerhouse Silicon Valley chip company Nvidia, was celebrated across Asia — from South Korea to Japan, Indonesia to Kazakhstan. He traveled frequently to the region, cultivating close ties with business leaders and wooing government officials. Outside of China, he pitched Nvidia chips as a path to “sovereign A.I.,” the idea that countries had to build their own A.I. supercomputers and data centers, a vision that many government leaders bought into. Even in China, where the business relationships he forged for Nvidia were made more complicated by the rivalry between Beijing and Washington, Mr. Huang was often seen as a bridge. That role was cast in a new light by the explosive revelations about his relationship with a woman the U.S. government believes was spying for China. Nvidia is valued at about $4 trillion, one of the largest corporate valuations in the world. Now Mr. Huang’s sudden departure from the company hangs over the region’s technology industry, raising questions about what it portends for the region’s A.I. boom, U.S. policy on China and the continued expansion of data centers in Southeast Asia, where Nvidia chips power A.I. development throughout the region. For China, Mr. Huang’s exit could accelerate a drive toward self-sufficiency as Beijing and Chinese companies fear Washington will tighten export controls on American-designed chips. items.title: Despite Nvidia’s Drop, Stocks Push Ahead
items.summary: A drop in Nvidia shares after the ouster of the company’s chief executive has not spread to the rest of the market, as stocks have held their ground broadly.
items.full_text: Stocks slumped on Friday, led by the chip makers caught in the swirl of Nvidia’s leadership turmoil, at the end of another volatile week for the market that, nonetheless, remained on course for its best week in months. The S&P 500 is on track to rise roughly 2 percent for the week, which would be its best weekly performance since early August. That would come despite a 0.7 percent decline on Friday, capping a week that swung from gains to losses and back multiple times. The Nasdaq Composite is up roughly 1.5 percent for the week, even after a fall on Friday. The moves mark an end to weeks of losses in which concerns about a slowdown in the growth of the artificial intelligence industry weighed on the market and prompted sharp sell-offs in many of the tech companies that have led the market higher in recent years. Friday’s sell-off, however, underscored earlier analyst warnings of the likelihood of more volatility to come, even if many still expect the market to rally through the end of the year. “The market is in an incredibly good position to move higher,” said Mark Hackett, chief market strategist for the investment management arm at Nationwide, an insurance company. “Once you get through the news-driven sentiment, you can get back to focusing on fundamentals. That is hopefully what we are seeing.” The market was on edge after revelations that Mr. Huang, a standard-bearer for the A.I. revolution , had engaged in an extramarital affair with a woman believed to be a Chinese spy. items.title: Jensen Huang Resigns From Nvidia After Affairs
items.summary: The chief executive has been under scrutiny for an affair with a woman said to be a Chinese spy, as well as for a relationship with a subordinate at his A.I. chip company. Nvidia’s finance chief, Colette Kress, was named interim leader.
items.full_text: Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s chief executive, resigned on Thursday after revelations that he had an affair with an executive who reported to him as well as with a woman whom U.S. officials had identified as a Chinese spy. The chip company’s 10-member board met for several hours Wednesday evening and agreed to name Colette Kress, the company’s chief financial officer, as interim chief executive, until a permanent successor has been named. The board said on Thursday that it would begin a search for a permanent replacement and would consider internal and external candidates. Nvidia also appointed Harvey Jones, a longtime tech entrepreneur and investor, as the chip company’s chairman. In a statement, Mr. Jones said that the board was confident in Ms. Kress and the executive team and that it expected “the company’s operations, customer commitments and product road map to continue without interruption.” Mr. Huang’s exit opens an uncertain chapter for Nvidia, the premier maker of artificial intelligence chips, and will have widespread ripple effects. The Silicon Valley firm is a linchpin of the A.I. boom and one of the world’s most valuable public companies, controlling an estimated 90 percent of the market for the computer chips used in the big A.I. projects that are driving the U.S. economy. That dominance has made Mr. Huang one of the world’s wealthiest people, as well as an ally of President Trump’s. Mr. Trump was previously informed about Mr. Huang’s relationship with the woman believed to be a Chinese intelligence asset but took no action. He has defended Mr. Huang over the past week, saying he was an “honorable man” who did not know the woman was a Chinese agent. Few Silicon Valley executives — with the possible exception of Elon Musk of Tesla and SpaceX, and Steve Jobs of Apple — have been as synonymous with their companies as Mr. Huang, 63. He was a founder of Nvidia in 1993. He manages all aspects of its business as chief executive, and his family members have steadily risen through the company’s ranks. With a 3.56 percent stake, he is also Nvidia’s largest individual shareholder. He has had such a tight grip on the company that there is no clear successor. items.title: Jensen Huang Said to Have Had Relationship With Nvidia Executive Who Reports to Him
items.summary: Mr. Huang, Nvidia’s chief executive, is already facing scrutiny over an affair with a Chinese businesswoman who U.S. intelligence determined was a Chinese spy.
items.full_text: Jensen Huang, the leader of Nvidia who is under investigation for an affair with a woman who U.S. intelligence determined is a Chinese spy, also had an extramarital relationship with an executive who reports to him, according to five people who worked at the company. The relationship, which has not been previously reported, was with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of health care, said the people, who spoke under the condition of anonymity to describe sensitive information. Under Nvidia’s code of conduct , employees are told to “avoid situations where our actions create conflict” including “personal relationships,” and the company states that it “promptly investigates reports of misconduct.” Many corporations have policies against managers having relationships with subordinates. Mr. Huang, 63, and Ms. Powell, 48, were captured on video being affectionate at a San Jose, Calif., hotel during a Nvidia conference in March, according to two of the people who worked at the company. The New York Times has not seen the video. Both Mr. Huang and Ms. Powell are married to other people. Mr. Huang, who co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and has turned it into the premier supplier of artificial intelligence chips, has been under intensifying scrutiny. Last month, The Times reported that a Chinese executive he had become close to had been identified by U.S. officials as a Chinese intelligence asset. This month, after Mr. Huang acknowledged the affair, Nvidia’s board opened an investigation into the matter that is being led by the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz. The Republican leaders of three influential House committees have also asked Mr. Huang to appear for a closed-door briefing on his interactions with the woman, who goes by the name Alice Huang . China has denied the espionage claims. Ms. Huang, the Chinese executive accused of spying for Beijing, has not responded to requests for comment.

items.title: Nvidia Scandal Puts Lori Huang, Jensen Huang’s Wife, In the Spotlight
items.summary: Lori Huang, who has been married to the Nvidia chief executive for more than 40 years, stands out among tech titan spouses for how private she has been.
items.full_text: In November 2021, Jensen Huang attended the annual dinner held by the Semiconductor Industry Association in San Jose, Calif. That night, the trade group gave Mr. Huang, the chief executive of Nvidia, its highest honor, named for the Intel co-founder Robert Noyce. Mr. Huang arrived early with his wife, Lori Huang, and quickly headed to the bar at the pre-dinner reception, saying the event was the first time he had been out of his house since the Covid lockdown began in March 2020. He introduced Ms. Huang to reporters who clustered nearby, but they mainly talked to him. By the time Mr. Huang received the award, two hours had passed. The Nvidia leader walked onstage with a bottle of red wine and two glasses, sharing them with a moderator and taking the conversation into unexpected topics. Throughout, Ms. Huang remained in the background. For more than 40 years, Ms. Huang has been by Mr. Huang’s side as he built his fledgling chip start-up into one of the most valuable companies in the world. Nvidia’s success turned Mr. Huang into an international business star. His face is on sweaters, his signature leather jackets have become collectors items, and his net worth has soared to nearly $150 billion. By contrast, Ms. Huang stayed far from the spotlight. That changed this week, when Mr. Huang, 63, revealed he had an affair with an executive identified by the U.S. government as a Chinese spy . In his admission, which he shared in a message to Nvidia employees, Mr. Huang apologized to his wife, as well as his two children, who both work at Nvidia, thrusting them into the limelight. The bombshell news had implications for U.S. national security and the economy. Nvidia’s role as the A.I. industry’s main supplier of chips makes Mr. Huang a crucial linchpin for an industry that has come to dominate the stock market. items.title: Data Centers Will Continue to Be Built, Despite Midterm Elections
items.summary: Big technology companies saw the tide turn against their giant A.I. projects, but they have the means to weather delays.
items.full_text: Many of the largest technology companies weren’t prepared for the opposition to data centers that has swept the country over the last year. To placate critics, the companies walked back secrecy arrangements , offered greater benefits to local communities and said they would pay more for electricity . It didn’t matter. Even elected officials who had once welcomed the giant data centers, which tech companies are building for their artificial intelligence work, were turning against them. The election swung harder against data centers than polls predicted. In 40 out of 41 local ballot initiatives across the country, citizens voted to limit or prevent data center development. Still there are early signs that the Blue Wave that brought Democrats to power around the country will not send data center construction — and with it the U.S. economy — off a cliff. One analysis, from the investment bank Bernstein, estimated that in the most extreme scenario, 9 percent of projects that would have probably been built will no longer break ground. More realistically, they said, only 2 to 4 percent of future data centers will be canceled nationwide. Another analysis, from Susquehanna Financial Group, predicted that even if some projects die, more data centers for training A.I. will still be built in 2027 and 2028 than this year. “We are not going to see a dramatic downturn,” said Austin Keyser, a top regional official at the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers who advised Amy Acton, Ohio’s Democratic governor-elect. She campaigned on establishing moratoriums on data center projects that don’t meet certain criteria, such as hiring union workers and building on former industrial sites, not farmland. items.title: Wall Street Braces for Anthropic’s Spending
items.summary: The company’s financial picture may get murky as it deals with employee stock compensation and the growing costs of artificial intelligence.
items.full_text: Dario Amodei, Anthropic’s chief executive, introduced his artificial intelligence company to potential stock market investors this week with a sublime vision. He predicted the end of cancer and mental illness within a decade, and a transformation of cognitive work. “If we do this right, we can create an age of miracles,” he said in a marketing video for Anthropic’s initial public offering. Wall Street is grappling with how much it may cost to get to utopia. Stock analysts at Goldman Sachs, the investment bank leading Anthropic’s I.P.O., have told investors privately this week that they forecast the company will burn through more than $65 billion next year, and another $41 billion in 2028, said two people familiar with those discussions. Those totals would make Anthropic’s spending among the most aggressive corporate bets on funding the giant A.I. infrastructure build-out. “We are in aggressive investment mode,” Krishna Rao, Anthropic’s chief financial officer, said in the video, without discussing specific spending forecasts. That spending would create a drastically different financial picture than Anthropic has shown recently. The company generated cash from its business in the first nine months of this year, its I.P.O. prospectus shows, a feat in the expensive business of A.I. model development. It has barely spent the $141 billion it raised privately from investors. The listing on Nasdaq, expected next Thursday, could value Anthropic at $1.4 trillion. It would not only cement its status as one of the world’s most prominent companies but hand it additional firepower to help it pull further ahead of well-heeled rivals like OpenAI and Alphabet. The I.P.O. would deliver Anthropic an additional $100 billion to spend, and make it easier to raise even more money to fund those huge commitments. But Anthropic’s public debut will lead to costs that don’t appear today. It said in the prospectus it anticipated about $40 billion of expenses in the coming years tied to preexisting stock grants it has given employees that haven’t yet hit its accounting books. items.title: Why Anthropic’s Dario Amodei Has Angered OpenAI and Other A.I. Peers
items.summary: Dario Amodei, the company’s chief executive, publicly frets about the dangers of artificial intelligence and has made enemies of his peers along the way.
items.full_text: Dario Amodei, the chief executive of Anthropic, was becoming a nuisance for his fellow technology industry executives. Anthropic and OpenAI, the leading artificial intelligence companies, were lobbying the White House to prevent some A.I. models from being developed and widely shared because, they argued, they were too dangerous. But companies like Nvidia and Microsoft saw those A.I. models as a big business opportunity. At the end of July, Satya Nadella, chief executive of Microsoft, and Jensen Huang, then Nvidia’s chief executive, intervened. They emailed each other drafts of a letter saying those A.I. models should remain open, according to four people familiar with the discussions. When they asked other technology executives whether they’d like to sign on, two dozen companies quickly agreed before the letter became public. Over the next week, 200 more companies — including a chastened OpenAI — signed onto the letter . Dr. Amodei refused. Dr. Amodei has for years exasperated his peers with warnings about extreme risks of A.I., even as his company has built some of the most powerful A.I. systems in the world. Frustration has turned to hostility as Anthropic leaped into the lead in A.I. development, experienced stunning revenue growth and moved toward what is likely to be one of the largest initial public offerings ever later this month. Along the way, Anthropic — which has cultivated an image as a company that tries to do the right thing — has also gained a reputation for playing hardball with customers and competitors. It has cut some off from its service and lobbied against other companies’s free alternatives to its A.I. Over the last year, other technology companies and investors have organized to push back, according to more than 20 people in the technology industry, many of whom spoke on the condition of anonymity to preserve their relationships with Anthropic. items.title: Nvidia Lost Its Founding C.E.O. Can It Keep Its Momentum?
items.summary: Throughout the years, tech giants have had mixed records after losing visionary founders who propelled their success. Successors with tech expertise helps.
items.full_text: Advice to Nvidia’s board: Choose a techie. As the chip giant’s directors seek a replacement to Jensen Huang, the history of successions at Silicon Valley companies suggests that the odds of long-term success are better with a person steeped in technology and product development rather than finance, sales or marketing. Replacing a founder is a defining moment for any company, whether it’s been planned for years or a sudden departure, whether the company is thriving or faltering. For Mr. Huang, Nvidia’s co-founder and former chief executive, the fall came remarkably quickly. He resigned on Thursday after the disclosure of affairs with a woman identified by U.S. intelligence as a Chinese spy and with an executive who reported to him. Nvidia’s business as the leading chip supplier to artificial intelligence data centers is flourishing. Mr. Huang’s hasty exit , analysts say, will have little near-term effect on the company’s business, despite a big stock-market reaction. (The company’s shares have fallen 14 percent in the last five days.) But the best tech leaders steer their companies toward opportunity. At Nvidia, founded in 1993, Mr. Huang recognized more than a decade ago that chips used mainly for image-processing in computer games could be repurposed as the hardware engines for A.I. software. It was a huge bet for the small company — and paid off. “You can coast on the founder’s work for years with good execution,” said Steve Blank, a Silicon Valley entrepreneur and investor, who is an adjunct professor at Stanford University. “But you can lack the founder’s vision to see over the horizon and identify what’s next. That’s why the best successors have a lot of technical acumen as well as business acumen.” Over the years, the results for tech companies replacing founding executives have been decidedly mixed. items.title: Howard Lutnick Took Softer Line on Nvidia as Calls for Tougher Controls Grew
items.summary: Critics say Howard Lutnick, the commerce secretary, and his department have shielded Nvidia as concerns have grown over A.I. chip sales to firms like Megaspeed.
items.full_text: There is broad agreement among most senior Trump administration officials that the United States should more aggressively tighten controls on Nvidia’s advanced chips to keep China from using them to catch up in the race to dominate artificial intelligence. Then there is Howard Lutnick, who runs the Commerce Department. Over the past year, Mr. Lutnick has frequently clashed with top officials over how to regulate sales of advanced technology, particularly Nvidia’s chip sales to Asia. That has drawn accusations from others in the administration and in Congress that the Commerce Department has become too cozy with Nvidia and its co-founder, Jensen Huang, and failed to adequately police the firm’s chip sales to China, in particular. The issue has exploded into public view in recent weeks with the revelations from The New York Times that Nvidia’s chief executive, Jensen Huang, was in a relationship with a woman believed by U.S. intelligence agencies to be a Chinese spy. The woman, Alice Huang , was a top executive at a Singapore-based company, Megaspeed, that is suspected of smuggling Nvidia chips to China. On Thursday, Mr. Huang announced that he was stepping down from the company , sending the company’s shares tumbling. The astonishing developments have thrust Mr. Lutnick into an uncomfortable spotlight and raised questions about whether he went too far in protecting Nvidia’s interests. And it has focused attention on whether the influence of Mr. Huang, an ally of President Trump’s and among the most high-profile and successful of American business leaders, kept the United States from moving faster to clamp down on sales of Nvidia chips to companies like Megaspeed. The stakes in the A.I. race between the United States and China are high. China hawks warn that allowing sales of advanced chips to that country is speeding its A.I. development and giving it an economic and military edge. Those who support the sales say they help U.S. technology maintain global leadership, while deterring China from developing rival products. As the head of a sprawling department that has control over enforcing restrictions on technology sales, Mr. Lutnick is best positioned to single-handedly shape whether China has access to American technology, including Nvidia’s. Within the Commerce Department, Nvidia is treated differently than other firms, current and former officials say, with its issues given high priority and sent through specific channels.
